module purpose: This module decodes supported shift commands from ctrl_i and shifts rs1_i by shamt_i, using either a serial shifter or a barrel shifter depending on FAST_SHIFT_EN. It buffers the shift result on res_o and drives valid_o when the implementation-defined command/result validity condition holds.

use-case flows.value: supported shift-command decision that enables this co-processor, starts the serial shifter, or marks a fast-path command as valid
serial shift operation: capture rs1_i and shamt_i, then decrement the count and shift the data left or right/arithmetic until completion
barrel shift operation: prepare the input word and sign-fill bit, apply shamt_i-selected shift stages, register the result, and drive it to res_o
result-valid / completion status on valid_o and result release gating for res_o
serial state and barrel-result buffer forced to zero while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow depends on the decision computed at lines 65-68: only the ctrl_i combinations matching the listed funct3/funct12 patterns with ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu = '1' assert valid_cmd. That decision is then consumed to set shifter.busy and load serial state at lines 87-95, to zero the barrel input when invalid at line 122, and to report fast-path validity at line 144. If this decision is corrupted, unsupported commands can start a shift or supported commands can be suppressed, so Integrity is established; Availability is also established because matching control values cause the module to accept the operation by those RTL conditions.

The operate flow uses shamt_i as the amount to apply: in the serial build, `shifter.cnt <= shamt_i;` at line 94 loads the amount, line 97 decrements it each step, and lines 108-109 read it to derive shifter.run and shifter.done; in the fast build, each shamt_i bit selects whether a barrel stage shifts at lines 128-129. If this value or state is corrupted, the module applies the wrong number of shift steps/stages and the produced result becomes incorrect, establishing Integrity. Availability is also established because the serial count is held in shifter.cnt until the run/done logic consumes it.

The module's main operate flow transforms rs1_i into the shift result under ctrl_i direction/sign control. In the serial build, lines 95 and 99/101 capture and update shifter.sreg, and line 111 forwards that stored value to res_o when the release condition holds; in the fast build, line 122 prepares the operand, line 123 forms the arithmetic sign-fill bit, line 138 registers bs_result, and line 143 drives res_o from that registered result. Corrupting this data breaks the implemented shift relation, so Integrity is established. Availability is also established because the result is stored in shifter.sreg or bs_result and delivered on res_o under the RTL-visible conditions.

The report flow depends on the module's decision that a shift result is ready. In the serial build, line 109 computes shifter.done from shifter.cnt, line 86 captures shifter.done_ff from `shifter.busy and shifter.done`, line 110 reports `valid_o <= shifter.busy and shifter.done`, and line 111 uses shifter.done_ff to release res_o; in the fast build, line 144 reports valid_o directly from valid_cmd. If this decision is corrupted, external logic can accept res_o at the wrong time or miss a completed result, establishing Integrity. Availability is also established because the serial logic produces completion from the stored count and the fast logic reports a qualified command immediately.
